analysis.file_name: A new strategy playbook for the US power industry.pdf
analysis.title: A new strategy playbook for the US power industry
key_insights: Hyperscalers treat securing power on time as a strategic priority. A data center waiting for power can lose as much as USD 10 billion in annual revenue per GW of computing capacity (a contract-based illustration from IREN's USD 9.7B Microsoft deal, not an industry average).

Rabobank projects US electricity consumption growth of up to 20% by 2030, driven predominantly by data centers. Data center construction takes 12 to 24 months, while some grid connections take three to seven years.
Large gas turbines can have delivery wait times of up to seven years. GE Vernova reports a global gas power equipment backlog and slot reservations totaling 116GW.

NVIDIA estimates its computing systems are roughly 60-70% (USD 35B) of the capital cost of an illustrative 1GW AI data center. Annual equipment depreciation could reach USD 7B on an assumed five-year straight-line life.

An on-site power premium of USD 10 to 75 per MWh over grid supply adds roughly USD 88M to USD 657M a year in operating cost at a continuous 1GW draw. Rabobank says the premium can be justified by the earnings from starting sooner.

Companies across the power value chain are using M&A to add scale, capabilities, and access to capital and customers. Examples are Constellation/Calpine, Alphabet/Intersect, the BlackRock GIP and EQT consortium/AES, NextEra/Dominion, and NRG/LS Power.
Constellation's combined fleet is 55GW, pairing nuclear with Calpine's gas plants, which can adjust output. NRG's purchase of about 13GW from LS Power is a similar expansion.
Acquiring operating plants changes ownership but does not add US generating capacity. New capacity requires restarting closed plants, expanding existing plants, and building new ones.

Gas plant acquisitions since September 2025 imply about USD 850 to 1,600 per kW (based on Cogentrix's portfolio and Hill Top). Lazard's July 2026 report quotes USD 2,400 to 2,600 per kW for new combined cycle plants entering service after 2028. Rabobank calls operating plants the low-hanging fruit.

Constellation plans to restart the closed 835MW Crane nuclear plant in Pennsylvania in 2027, backed by its agreement with Microsoft. Vistra has agreements with Meta supporting 433MW of added nuclear capacity through upgrades, with full delivery by 2034.
NextEra plans up to 10GW of new gas generation in Texas and Pennsylvania, with initial capacity as early as the end of 2028 and completion in 2032.

The proposed NextEra/Dominion combination would serve about 10 million utility customer accounts and own 110GW of generation. It needs state utility commission and federal approvals, and its case rests partly on limiting costs passed to ratepayers.
AES has 11.8GW of signed supply agreements with major technology companies. The BlackRock GIP and EQT-led consortium would fund its project pipeline.

Rabobank expects suppliers to evolve into long-term energy partners that commit to a data center's power needs within agreed reliability, timing, and cost terms. It expects the premium for immediate power access to ease as supply catches up in individual markets.

sector_views.rationale: Rising data center demand and long-term power purchase commitments give companies with available generation in high-demand locations an immediate opportunity. The report does not issue a formal rating.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Data center demand is expanding the market for US power companies faster than generation and grid supply can be delivered.

risk_factors: Delayed power delivery cuts data center revenue and the time available to recover investment before newer chips make installed equipment less competitive.
Gas turbine delivery waits of up to seven years and grid connection waits of three to seven years limit new supply.
Planned projects remain subject to approvals and construction. NextEra/Dominion needs state and federal approvals.
Infrastructure expansion is pressuring electricity bills, which could limit cost recovery.
Acquisitions of operating plants do not add generating capacity, so supply may lag demand.

theme_stances.theme: power supply integration for data centers
theme_stances.key_argument: Suppliers and hyperscalers are building integrated platforms that combine power supply with customer access, and suppliers will evolve into long-term energy partners.
theme_stances.evidence: We expect the emerging supplier platforms to evolve toward an integrated energy-service model.
